items.title: The user takes the text box on focus, releases on blur or close
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-07 (musing "Desk Improvement: User creates goals and items without agents present"): "the text box in item/goal detail must be an input area for the user. When the user activates that input area, the area is \"taken\" by the user, and not modifiable for agents. When the user clicks outside of that text box, and deactivates the input, also by leaving the details dialog, the box input is released from the take. When a details dialog is opened, the text box is never taken."

Today: box.take refuses andy by name; a take is freed only by the taker's box.write. Shape: box.take accepts andy; a new release (box.release {id}) frees a take without a write; the dialog takes on focus, releases on blur and on close. Agents' box.write is refused taken while his take stands, as it is for an agent's take today.

Andy, 2026-10-07, on Q1 (does his take refuse an agent's box.write until he leaves the box, even when he types nothing): "yes. so it shoule be among agents as well, the box is taken, and released after edit. it also helps agents stay out of each others way."
So: one take rule for everybody. Focus takes, the edit's end releases; while a take stands every other writer, agent or not, is refused taken.

items.title: A split adds only the explicit blocking relation
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-07 (musing "Desk Improvement: User creates goals and items without agents present"): "when splitting an item, only the new explicit blocking relationship is automatically added, the implicit blocking will not need to be specified, it clutters the list display with confusing \"blocks\" and \"waits on\" columns, and is not needed for a dependency graph."

Today: blocks come from the session json an agent sends; on 2026-10-03 Andy ruled the new items block the parent. Andy, 2026-10-07, on Q1 (which relation is the explicit one): "the new split-items always block the item from which they were split, items blocked by the current item are still blocked by the newly split item, because if theyre blocked by me, they are implicitly blocked by the newly created/split item."
Shape: a split writes one relation per new item, new item blocks parent, and nothing else; what the parent blocks stays the parent's and reaches the new item through it. The 2026-10-03 ruling stands, this names what is NOT written.

items.title: The desk owns goal and item ids
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-07 (musing "Desk Improvement: User creates goals and items without agents present"): "the desk owns (is in charge of) goal and item ID's."

Today: ids are named by the agent inside the session.set json (goal/G9.1 and so on). Shape: the desk mints the next id itself for anything added through goal.add and item.add (G9.10, G9.11); Andy, 2026-10-07, on Q1 (do agents keep naming ids in session.set): "why should the agents need to, they can use the same api's the user needs to create them."
